Ovid's Metamorphoses is a long mythological poem compiled by Publius Ovidius Naso, a Roman poet born in 43 BCE. The poem details a multitude of myths, traditionally arranged into fifteen books, each detailing a particular myth or series of myths populated by figures from Greek and Roman mythology. Though the poem explores many themes, the overarching subject is transformation, or metamorphosis, as the title would suggest. Ovid traces the history of the world from its creation to his own day, incorporating individual myths along the way. The poem is famous both for its extensive breadth and for the rhetorical flare Ovid brings to each tale.
